intro: On Monday your manager calls: 'I'm busy today. I'll call you tomorrow.' A week later a colleague asks what he said, and 'He says he is busy today' doesn't work any more. In this lesson you learn to report what people said later, with said and told, and to change tenses, pronouns and time words. Warm-up: would you start with 'He said me…' or 'He told me…'?
teachingNotes: Build on a2-mediation-messages: there the learner passed on a message right away with says and changed I → he/she, my → his/her (Sari says she's sick). Recap that in one line. New here: reporting LATER with said/told, which moves the tense back and changes time and place words. Statements only. Reported questions (She asked where I lived) and commands (He told me to wait) are a note for a later lesson; don't drill them.

say vs tell: tell needs a person right after it (told me / told us / told Pak Hasan); say has no person after it (said that…), or uses to (said to me, correct but less common than told me). Common errors: 'She said me that she was tired.' → 'She told me that she was tired.'; 'He told that he was busy.' → 'He said that he was busy.' that is optional after both. Indonesian 'bilang (ke saya)' covers both verbs, which causes the errors. said is pronounced like 'sed', not 'seid'. If asked: tell a story / a lie / the truth are fixed phrases without a person.

Backshift (keep to this list): am/is → was, are → were, present simple → past simple (work → worked, don't/doesn't → didn't), will → would (won't → wouldn't), can → could (can't → couldn't), past simple → had + past participle (went → had gone; the past perfect from b1-past-perfect). Why: the words were spoken in the past, so they move one step back. Indonesian never changes the verb (Dia bilang dia capek), so learners keep the present. Don't teach backshift of the present continuous, present perfect or modals like must/may/should; if the learner asks, say it comes later.

Past simple → had + past participle is the textbook rule, but in everyday speech the past simple often stays (She said she lost her phone). Accept that as natural if the learner uses it, while teaching had + past participle because it makes the order of events clear. In questions, test it only where the options make the had form the only good one.

Pronouns and time/place words: I → he/she, my → his/her, me → him/her, we → they, our → their, and you → me/I when the message was for the reporter. today → that day, tomorrow → the next day (or the following day), yesterday → the day before (or the previous day), here → there. Common error: '(reporting a week later) She said she will come tomorrow.' → 'She said she would come the next day.'

When nothing changes: reporting right now with says (She says she's in the lobby), on the same day (today can stay today), or a fact that is still true (He said the office opens at eight is fine). Mention this but test only clear cases: every question says the report is LATER (a week later, last month) and the situation is over, so the backshift is the only right answer. would and could: the l is silent ('wud', 'kud').

keyPoints.title: said or told?
keyPoints.explanation: When you report later, use said or told. tell needs a person right after it: She told me (that)… say has no person after it: She said (that)… or She said to me… So 'said me' and 'told that' are wrong. that can be left out.

examples.en: She told me that she was tired.
examples.id: Dia bilang ke aku bahwa dia capek.

examples.en: He said that he was busy.
Pak Hasan told the team the client was happy.
examples.id: Pak Hasan memberi tahu tim bahwa kliennya senang.

id.title: said atau told?
id.explanation: Kalau kamu melaporkan ucapan orang belakangan, pakai said atau told. tell harus langsung diikuti orang: She told me (that)… say tidak diikuti orang: She said (that)… atau She said to me… Jadi 'said me' dan 'told that' salah. that boleh dihilangkan.

keyPoints.title: One step back in the past
keyPoints.explanation: The words were said in the past, so when you report them later the verb moves one step back: am/is → was, are → were, work → worked, don't → didn't, will → would, can → could, and past simple → had + past participle (went → had gone).

examples.en: Budi said he would bring the projector.
Bu Ani said she had forgotten her laptop.
examples.id: Bu Ani: 'Laptop saya ketinggalan.' (forgot → had forgotten)

id.title: Mundur satu langkah ke masa lampau
id.explanation: Kata-katanya diucapkan di masa lalu, jadi saat kamu melaporkannya belakangan, kata kerjanya mundur satu langkah: am/is → was, are → were, work → worked, don't → didn't, will → would, can → could, dan past simple → had + past participle (went → had gone).

keyPoints.title: Change the people, the place and the day
keyPoints.explanation: Use your point of view: I → he/she, my → his/her, we → they, me → him/her (and you → me if they were talking to you). Time and place words change too: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there.

examples.en: Sari said she was at the office that day.
examples.id: Sari: 'Saya di kantor hari ini.' (I → she, today → that day)

examples.en: Dimas said he would call me the next day.
examples.id: Dimas: 'Saya telepon kamu besok.' (you → me, tomorrow → the next day)

examples.en: They said they had arrived the day before.
examples.id: Mereka: 'Kami sampai kemarin.' (we → they, yesterday → the day before)

id.title: Ubah orangnya, tempatnya dan harinya
id.explanation: Pakai sudut pandangmu sendiri: I → he/she, my → his/her, we → they, me → him/her (dan you → me kalau dia bicara kepadamu). Keterangan waktu dan tempat juga berubah: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with said or told: Dimas ___ me that the printer was broken.
guidedPractice.hint: There's a person (me) right after the gap, so use tell → told.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with said or told: Bu Ani ___ that the lift wasn't working.
guidedPractice.hint: No person after the gap, so use say → said.

guidedPractice.prompt: Last Friday Budi and Sari said: 'We are ready for the presentation.' A week later: They said they ___ ready for the presentation.
guidedPractice.hint: are moves one step back to were.

guidedPractice.prompt: Last year, at a hotel in Lombok, Rina said: 'I'm so happy here.' Today you tell a friend: Rina said she was so happy ___.
guidedPractice.hint: You're not in that hotel now, so here → there.

independentPractice.prompt: Last Tuesday Dimas said: 'I don't understand the new app.' A week later: Dimas said he ___ the new app.
independentPractice.hint: don't moves back to didn't; understand stays in its base form after didn't.

independentPractice.prompt: Last month Bu Ani said: 'I lost my ID card.' Report it: Bu Ani said she ___ her ID card.
independentPractice.hint: Past simple → had + past participle: lose, lost, lost.

independentPractice.prompt: Last week Budi told you: 'I'll send you the file tomorrow.' Report it: Budi told me he would send me the file ___.
independentPractice.hint: A week later, 'tomorrow' isn't tomorrow any more.

assessment.prompt: Complete with said or told: At the morning meeting, Pak Hasan ___ us that the client was happy with the design.
assessment.rubric: Correct: told (a person, us, comes right after the gap, so tell). 'said' = 0 ('said us' is the error this lesson targets; say has no person after it). 'tells' or 'tell' = 40 (right verb, but the meeting is over, so the past: told).

assessment.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Write it correctly: Rina said me that she was tired.
acceptableAnswers: rina told me that she was tired
rina told me she was tired
rina said that she was tired
rina said to me that she was tired
rina said to me she was tired
assessment.rubric: Correct: Rina told me (that) she was tired, or Rina said (to me) (that) she was tired. 'Rina told that she was tired' = 30 (tell needs a person). 'Rina told me that she is tired' = 70 (say/tell fixed, but the tense should stay was). Rewriting the sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Last Monday Sari called you from the KRL: 'I'm at Manggarai station.' A week later you tell Emma about the call. Complete with one word: Sari said she ___ at Manggarai station.
assessment.rubric: Correct: was (am → was; the call was a week ago and she isn't there now). 'is' = 30 (no tense change: the trap from Indonesian, which never changes the verb). 'were' = 40 (moved back, but she takes was).

assessment.prompt: A week ago Bu Ani texted the team: 'I'll be late for the meeting.' Today your manager asks why she was late. Complete: Bu Ani said she ___ be late for the meeting.
assessment.rubric: Correct: would (will → would; the meeting was a week ago). 'will' = 30 (no tense change). 'was' or 'is going to' = 20 (not the will → would change).

assessment.prompt: Last month Dimas said: 'I can't come to the office party.' The party was two weeks ago. Complete: Dimas said he ___ come to the office party.
assessment.rubric: Correct: couldn't / could not (can't → couldn't). 'can't' = 30 (no tense change). 'could' = 20 (moved back, but lost the not: the meaning is the opposite). 'didn't can' = 10.

assessment.prompt: Two weeks ago Rina told you: 'I have a job interview today.' Report it in one English sentence. Start with: Rina said
acceptableAnswers: rina said she had a job interview that day
rina said that she had a job interview that day
rina said she had a job interview on that day
rina said that she had a job interview on that day
rina said she had an interview that day
rina said that she had an interview that day
assessment.rubric: Correct: Rina said (that) she had a job interview that day (I → she, have → had, today → that day). 'today' instead of 'that day' = 50. 'I had' instead of 'she had' = 40. 'has' instead of 'had' = 50. 'an interview' instead of 'a job interview' is fine.

assessment.prompt: Last Monday Budi said: 'We are free tomorrow.' Now it's a week later. Complete with the right time words: Budi said they were free ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: the next day (or the following day): a week later, 'tomorrow' would mean a different day. 'tomorrow' = 0 (the error this lesson targets). 'the day before' = 0 (that's for yesterday). 'next day' without the = 80.

blocks.text:
In A2 you passed on a message **right away**, with *says*: *Sari says she's sick.* Now you report what someone said **earlier**: an hour ago, last week, last month. This is called **reported speech**: telling someone what another person said, in your own words (not with quote marks). For that you use the past: **said** or **told**.

Both mean *bilang*, but they work differently:
- **tell → told** needs a **person** right after it: *She **told me** that…*, *He **told the team** that…*, *Bu Ani **told Pak Hasan** that…*
- **say → said** has **no person** after it: *She **said** that…* If you want to name the person, add **to**: *She said **to me** that…* (correct, but *told me* is more common).

So the two classic mistakes are *She said me…* ✗ and *He told that…* ✗. The word **that** is optional after both: *She told me (that) she was tired.*

id.text:
Di A2 kamu menyampaikan pesan **langsung saat itu**, dengan *says*: *Sari says she's sick.* Sekarang kamu melaporkan apa yang dikatakan seseorang **sebelumnya**: sejam lalu, minggu lalu, bulan lalu. Ini disebut **reported speech** (kalimat tidak langsung): menceritakan ke orang lain apa yang dikatakan seseorang, dengan kata-katamu sendiri (bukan dengan tanda kutip). Untuk itu kamu memakai bentuk lampau: **said** atau **told**.

Keduanya berarti *bilang*, tapi cara pakainya beda:
- **tell → told** harus langsung diikuti **orang**: *She **told me** that…*, *He **told the team** that…*, *Bu Ani **told Pak Hasan** that…*
- **say → said** **tidak** diikuti orang: *She **said** that…* Kalau mau menyebut orangnya, tambahkan **to**: *She said **to me** that…* (benar, tapi *told me* lebih umum).

Jadi dua kesalahan klasiknya adalah *She said me…* ✗ dan *He told that…* ✗. Kata **that** (= bahwa) boleh dipakai, boleh tidak, setelah keduanya: *She told me (that) she was tired.*

rows.en: Rina said that she was tired.
Rina told me that she was tired.
rows.id: Rina bilang ke aku bahwa dia capek.

rows.en: Pak Hasan told the team the client was happy.
rows.id: Pak Hasan memberi tahu tim bahwa kliennya senang.

rows.en: Dimas said to me that he was hungry.
rows.id: Dimas bilang ke aku bahwa dia lapar.
rows.note: said to + person: correct, less common

id.note: said to + orang: benar, tapi lebih jarang

blocks.text:
**The bilang trap.** Indonesian *bilang* works with or without a person: *Dia bilang…* and *Dia bilang ke saya…*. English splits it: no person → **said**; person → **told** + person. Quick test: is there *me, us, him, her* or a name right after the verb? Then it's **told**.

Pronunciation: **said** sounds like *sed* (rhymes with *red*), not *seid*. And remember the fixed phrases **tell a story, tell a lie, tell the truth**: there *tell* has no person.

id.text:
**Jebakan kata bilang.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *bilang* bisa dipakai dengan atau tanpa orang: *Dia bilang…* dan *Dia bilang ke saya…*. Bahasa Inggris memisahkannya: tanpa orang → **said**; ada orang → **told** + orang. Tes cepat: apakah ada *me, us, him, her* atau nama orang langsung setelah kata kerjanya? Kalau ya, pakai **told**.

Pengucapan: **said** dibaca *sed* (seperti *red*), bukan *seid*. Ingat juga ungkapan tetap **tell a story, tell a lie, tell the truth** (bercerita, berbohong, berkata jujur): di sini *tell* tidak diikuti orang.

blocks.prompt: Budi ___ that the KRL was very crowded this morning.
blocks.explain: There's no person after the gap, so use **said**. *told* needs a person right after it (*told me, told us*), so *Budi told that…* is wrong.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Budi ___ that the KRL was very crowded this morning.
id.explain: Tidak ada orang setelah titik-titiknya, jadi pakai **said**. *told* harus langsung diikuti orang (*told me, told us*), jadi *Budi told that…* salah.

material.title: One step back in the past

blocks.text:
On Monday Rina says: *'I **am** tired.'* A week later she's fine, and a colleague asks about her. If you say *Rina said she **is** tired*, it sounds like she's tired **now**. The words were said in the **past**, so when you report them later, the verb moves **one step back** into the past. Grammar books call this **backshift** (= mundur satu langkah):
- **am / is → was**: *'I am tired.'* → *She said she **was** tired.*
- **are → were**: *'We are late.'* → *They said they **were** late.*
- **present simple → past simple**: *'I work late.'* → *He said he **worked** late.* *'I don't know.'* → *She said she **didn't** know.*
- **will → would** (won't → wouldn't): *'I'll call.'* → *He said he **would** call.*
- **can → could** (can't → couldn't): *'I can help.'* → *She said she **could** help.*
- **past simple → had + past participle** (the past perfect from the last lesson): *'I forgot.'* → *She said she **had forgotten**.* It goes one step further back, because the forgetting happened **before** she spoke.

id.text:
Hari Senin Rina bilang: *'I **am** tired.'* Seminggu kemudian dia sudah sehat, dan seorang rekan kerja bertanya tentang dia. Kalau kamu bilang *Rina said she **is** tired*, kedengarannya dia capek **sekarang**. Kata-katanya diucapkan di **masa lalu**, jadi saat kamu melaporkannya belakangan, kata kerjanya **mundur satu langkah** ke masa lampau. Buku tata bahasa menyebutnya **backshift** (= mundur satu langkah):
- **am / is → was**: *'I am tired.'* → *She said she **was** tired.*
- **are → were**: *'We are late.'* → *They said they **were** late.*
- **present simple → past simple**: *'I work late.'* → *He said he **worked** late.* *'I don't know.'* → *She said she **didn't** know.*
- **will → would** (won't → wouldn't): *'I'll call.'* → *He said he **would** call.*
- **can → could** (can't → couldn't): *'I can help.'* → *She said she **could** help.*
- **past simple → had + past participle** (past perfect dari pelajaran sebelumnya): *'I forgot.'* → *She said she **had forgotten**.* Ini mundur satu langkah lagi, karena kejadian lupa itu terjadi **sebelum** dia bicara.

rows.en: Pak Hasan said he was in a meeting.
The interns said they were hungry.
Sari said she liked the new office.
Budi said he would bring the projector.
Bu Ani said she couldn't find her keys.
rows.id: Bu Ani: 'Saya tidak bisa menemukan kunci saya.'

rows.en: Dimas said he had missed the bus.

blocks.text:
**Indonesian never changes the verb**: *Dia bilang dia capek* is the same on Monday and a week later. So the most common mistake is keeping the present: *(a week later) She said she **is** tired* ✗ → *was*. When you see **said** or **told** and the moment is over, move the verb back.

Two small notes: **would** and **could** have a silent *l* (say *wud*, *kud*). And with the past simple, many people just keep it in everyday speech (*She said she forgot*). That's OK when talking, but **had + past participle** makes the order clear, so learn that one.

id.text:
**Bahasa Indonesia tidak pernah mengubah kata kerjanya**: *Dia bilang dia capek* sama saja hari Senin maupun seminggu kemudian. Jadi kesalahan paling umum adalah tetap memakai bentuk sekarang: *(seminggu kemudian) She said she **is** tired* ✗ → *was*. Kalau kamu melihat **said** atau **told** dan momennya sudah lewat, mundurkan kata kerjanya.

Dua catatan kecil: **would** dan **could** huruf *l*-nya tidak dibaca (ucapkan *wud*, *kud*). Dan untuk past simple, banyak orang membiarkannya saja dalam percakapan sehari-hari (*She said she forgot*). Itu tidak apa-apa saat ngobrol, tapi **had + past participle** membuat urutan kejadiannya jelas, jadi pelajari bentuk itu.

blocks.prompt: Last Monday Rina said: 'I am sick.' Now it's Friday and she's fine. You tell Emma: Rina said she ___ sick.
blocks.explain: The words were said on Monday and she isn't sick now, so **am → was**. *is* sounds like she's still sick; *were* doesn't go with *she*.

id.prompt: Senin lalu Rina bilang: 'I am sick.' Sekarang hari Jumat dan dia sudah sehat. Kamu bilang ke Emma: Rina said she ___ sick.
id.explain: Kata-katanya diucapkan hari Senin dan sekarang dia tidak sakit, jadi **am → was**. *is* terdengar seolah dia masih sakit; *were* tidak cocok dengan *she*.

id.title: Mundur satu langkah ke masa lampau

material.title: Change the people, the place and the day

blocks.text:
The message is in the **speaker's** words. When you report it, you use **your** point of view, like in A2:
- **I → he / she**, **my → his / her**, **me → him / her**, **we → they**, **our → their**
- **you → me / I** when the message was for **you**: Dimas to you: *'I'll call **you**.'* → *Dimas said he would call **me**.*

Words for **time** and **place** change too, for the same reason. On Monday, *tomorrow* meant Tuesday. If you say *tomorrow* a week later, people think of a different day. So:
- **today → that day**
- **tomorrow → the next day** (or *the following day*)
- **yesterday → the day before** (or *the previous day*)
- **here → there** (when you're not in that place any more)

The classic mistake: *(a week later) She said she will come tomorrow* ✗ → *She said she **would** come **the next day**.*

id.text:
Pesannya memakai kata-kata **si pembicara**. Saat kamu melaporkannya, pakai sudut pandang **kamu sendiri**, seperti di A2:
- **I → he / she**, **my → his / her**, **me → him / her**, **we → they**, **our → their**
- **you → me / I** kalau pesannya untuk **kamu**: Dimas kepadamu: *'I'll call **you**.'* → *Dimas said he would call **me**.*

Kata untuk **waktu** dan **tempat** juga berubah, dengan alasan yang sama. Hari Senin, *tomorrow* (besok) berarti Selasa. Kalau kamu bilang *tomorrow* seminggu kemudian, orang akan memikirkan hari yang lain. Jadi:
- **today → that day** (hari itu)
- **tomorrow → the next day** (atau *the following day*; keesokan harinya)
- **yesterday → the day before** (atau *the previous day*; sehari sebelumnya)
- **here → there** (di sini → di sana, kalau kamu sudah tidak di tempat itu)

Kesalahan klasiknya: *(seminggu kemudian) She said she will come tomorrow* ✗ → *She said she **would** come **the next day**.*

rows.en: Sari said she was at the office that day.
Dimas said he would call me the next day.
rows.note: you → me; tomorrow → the next day

id.note: you → me; tomorrow → the next day

rows.en: They said they had arrived the day before.
rows.note: we → they; yesterday → the day before

id.note: we → they; yesterday → the day before

rows.en: Pak Hasan said the coffee there was great.
rows.id: Pak Hasan (di Bandung): 'Kopi di sini enak sekali.'

blocks.text: Check the **owner** words too, like in A2: Indonesian *dia* and *-nya* are the same for a man and a woman, but English must choose. Sari, Rina, Bu Ani → **she / her**; Budi, Dimas, Pak Hasan → **he / his / him**.

id.text: Cek juga kata **pemilik**, seperti di A2: *dia* dan *-nya* dalam bahasa Indonesia sama untuk laki-laki dan perempuan, tapi bahasa Inggris harus memilih. Sari, Rina, Bu Ani → **she / her**; Budi, Dimas, Pak Hasan → **he / his / him**.

blocks.prompt: Last year, on holiday in Bali, Sari said: 'I love it here.' Today you tell a friend in Jakarta: Sari said she loved it ___.
blocks.explain: You're in Jakarta, not in Bali, so **here → there**. *here* would mean Jakarta, and *that* isn't a place word.

id.prompt: Tahun lalu, saat liburan di Bali, Sari bilang: 'I love it here.' Hari ini kamu cerita ke teman di Jakarta: Sari said she loved it ___.
id.explain: Kamu di Jakarta, bukan di Bali, jadi **here → there**. *here* berarti Jakarta, dan *that* bukan kata untuk tempat.

material.title: When nothing changes, and what comes later

blocks.text:
You don't always move everything back:
- **Right now, with says**: the person is still on the phone or just texted. Use **says** and keep the present, like in A2: *Rina **says** she**'s** in the lobby.*
- **Still true**: *'The office opens at eight.'* → *He said the office **opens** at eight* is fine, because it still opens at eight. (*opened* is fine too.)
- **The same day**: if Rina said *today* this morning, *today* still means today.

But when you report **later** and the situation is **over** (she isn't tired any more, *tomorrow* has passed), change the tense and the words. In this lesson's questions we always say when you're reporting (*a week later, last month*), so you know.

**Coming later:** reported **questions** (*'Where do you live?'* → *She **asked** where I **lived***) and **orders or requests** (*'Wait here.'* → *He **told me to wait** there*). You'll practise those in a later lesson.

id.text:
Kamu tidak selalu harus memundurkan semuanya:
- **Saat itu juga, dengan says**: orangnya masih di telepon atau baru saja kirim pesan. Pakai **says** dan tetap bentuk sekarang, seperti di A2: *Rina **says** she**'s** in the lobby.*
- **Masih benar**: *'The office opens at eight.'* → *He said the office **opens** at eight* boleh, karena kantornya memang masih buka jam delapan. (*opened* juga boleh.)
- **Di hari yang sama**: kalau Rina bilang *today* tadi pagi, *today* masih berarti hari ini.

Tapi kalau kamu melaporkan **belakangan** dan situasinya sudah **lewat** (dia sudah tidak capek, *besok*-nya sudah lewat), ubah tense dan kata-katanya. Di soal-soal pelajaran ini kami selalu menyebutkan kapan kamu melapor (*a week later, last month*), jadi kamu tahu.

**Nanti di pelajaran lain:** **pertanyaan** yang dilaporkan (*'Where do you live?'* → *She **asked** where I **lived***) dan **perintah atau permintaan** (*'Wait here.'* → *He **told me to wait** there*). Itu akan kamu latih di pelajaran berikutnya.

rows.en: Rina says she's in the lobby.

id.note: saat itu juga: says + bentuk sekarang

rows.en: Rina said she was in the lobby.
He said the office opens at eight.
rows.note: still true: the present is fine

blocks.prompt: Rina is on the phone with you right now: 'I'm at the gate.' You tell Budi, who is next to you: Rina ___ she's at the gate.
blocks.explain: She's speaking **right now**, so use **says** + the present (*she's*). *tells* and *told* need a person right after them (*tells me, told us*).

id.prompt: Rina sedang menelepon kamu sekarang: 'I'm at the gate.' Kamu bilang ke Budi yang ada di sebelahmu: Rina ___ she's at the gate.
id.explain: Dia bicara **sekarang**, jadi pakai **says** + bentuk sekarang (*she's*). *tells* dan *told* harus langsung diikuti orang (*tells me, told us*).

resources.note: Explanation and two online exercises at B1–B2 level: tense changes, when the tense can stay, and time and place words. It also covers a few tenses this lesson leaves for later.

id.note: Penjelasan dan dua latihan online untuk level B1–B2: perubahan tense, kapan tense boleh tetap, dan keterangan waktu dan tempat. Ada juga beberapa tense yang di pelajaran ini disimpan untuk nanti.

flashcards.front: Dia bilang ke aku bahwa dia capek.
flashcards.back: She told me (that) she was tired.
No: said (that)… / said to me… / told me…
had forgotten (past simple → had + past participle)

id.intro: Hari Senin manajermu menelepon: 'I'm busy today. I'll call you tomorrow.' Seminggu kemudian seorang rekan kerja bertanya apa katanya, dan 'He says he is busy today' sudah tidak cocok lagi. Di pelajaran ini kamu belajar melaporkan ucapan orang belakangan, dengan said dan told, serta mengubah tense, kata ganti dan keterangan waktu. Pemanasan: kamu akan mulai dengan 'He said me…' atau 'He told me…'?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'am' berubah jadi 'was' saat aku melaporkan ucapan orang?
Bagaimana melaporkan pertanyaan, seperti 'Where do you live?'

assessment.rsp-1: Lengkapi dengan said atau told: At the morning meeting, Pak Hasan ___ us that the client was happy with the design.
assessment.rsp-2: Kalimat ini ada kesalahannya. Tulis kalimat yang benar: Rina said me that she was tired.
assessment.rsp-3: Senin lalu Sari meneleponmu dari KRL: 'I'm at Manggarai station.' Seminggu kemudian kamu cerita ke Emma tentang telepon itu. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Sari said she ___ at Manggarai station.
assessment.rsp-4: Seminggu lalu Bu Ani mengirim pesan ke tim: 'I'll be late for the meeting.' Hari ini manajermu bertanya kenapa dia terlambat. Lengkapi: Bu Ani said she ___ be late for the meeting.
assessment.rsp-5: Bulan lalu Dimas bilang: 'I can't come to the office party.' Pestanya sudah lewat dua minggu lalu. Lengkapi: Dimas said he ___ come to the office party.
assessment.rsp-6: Dua minggu lalu Rina bilang kepadamu: 'I have a job interview today.' Laporkan ucapannya dalam satu kalimat bahasa Inggris. Mulai dengan: Rina said
assessment.rsp-7: Senin lalu Budi bilang: 'We are free tomorrow.' Sekarang sudah seminggu kemudian. Lengkapi dengan keterangan waktu yang tepat: Budi said they were free ___.
